title: HAAF — area-based hypo memory and counterregulation gate (Cryer / Dagogo-Jack)

caption.scope: Hypoglycemia-Associated Autonomic Failure (HAAF; Cryer 1992, Cryer et al. 2003) is modelled as an area-based memory rather than a discrete episode count. When BG falls below 3.0 mmol/L, hypoArea accumulates proportionally to depth × duration; when BG stays above 4.0 mmol/L it decays with t½ ≈ 3 simulated days (calibrated to Dagogo-Jack et al., J Clin Invest 91:819-828, 1993 and Cranston et al., Lancet 344:283-287, 1994). The accumulated burden passes through a sigmoid that produces counterRegFactor between 0.3 and 1.0. This factor multiplies the acute stress amplitude — modelled here as the gate factor multiplying acute stress amplitude in the stress multiplier — so repeated hypoglycemia progressively blunts the catecholamine/glucagon rescue response. Acute stress in T1D is already capped at 0.4 (vs ~5.0 healthy) due to absent glucagon secretion; HAAF further reduces what little counter-regulatory reserve remains.

variables.definition: cumulative hypo burden (mmol·min equivalent); accumulates at rate max(0, 3.0 − BG) while BG < 3.0 mmol/L
counter-regulatory gate output: 0.3 + 0.7 · exp(−hypoArea / 30); range [0.3, 1.0]; floor at 0.3 (blunting is never complete)
triggering condition for hypo memory accumulation (hypo threshold)
triggering condition for hypo memory decay (recovery threshold)
incremental hypoArea accumulation rate — proportional to hypoglycemia depth and proportional to simulated time step dt
hypoArea decay toward zero with half-life ≈ 3 simulated days when BG > 4.0 mmol/L; parameterised as ln(2)/4320 per sim-minute
sigmoid mapping hypoArea to counterRegFactor; scale constant 30 calibrated so BG 2.5 for 20 min yields ~20 % reduction (Dagogo-Jack 1993)
counterRegFactor applied as multiplicative scalar to acute stress amplitude in the stress multiplier sum
acute stress amplitude modulated by counterRegFactor; feeds directly into the stressMultiplier term used in EGP = EGP₀ · max(0, stressMultiplier − x3)
